newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA PRESSES PRIVATE FIRMS TO LEAVE GAS JV.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA PRESSES PRIVATE FIRMS TO LEAVE GAS JV.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet decided on Thursday to ask private firms in Bulgarian-Russian joint gas stock company Topenergy to transfer their shares to state-owned Bulgargas in a bid to restore its 50 percent participation.

Deputy Prime Minister Evgenii Bakardzhiev said that under an intergovernmental agreement between Bulgaria and Russia signed in 1994, only state firms could share Bulgaria's 50 percent stake in Topenergy, set up to deliver Russian natural gas to the Balkans.

"The cabinet took a decision that representatives of Bulgargas should submit a proposal to Topenergy's general meeting according to which Multigroup, Overgas Inc, First Private Bank and Chimimport transfer their shares to Bulgargas," he told a news conference.
If the private shareholders, which include powerful conglomerate Multigroup, reject the proposal, the cabinet agreed to approve establishment of a new joint gas company with Russia.

"If they reject (the proposal), the cabinet agrees that Bulgargas representatives submit a proposal for holding a new general meeting which will take a decision to terminate Topenergy's activities and to establish a new Bulgarian-Russian venture," Bakardzhiev said.
A two thirds majority will be needed for taking a decision for liquidation of the company, Bakardzhiev told a local daily newspaper Standart in an interview on Thursday.
Topenergy was established by Russia's Gazprom and Bulgaria's gas monopolist Bulgargas in 1995.
The two sides initially held equal shares. But in November 1995 Topenergy doubled its capital to 120 million levs and it admitted new Bulgarian shareholders in 1996.
Gazprom kept its 50 percent stake, while Bulgargas's share dropped to 25.1 percent from an original 50 percent.

Multigroup and its gas arm Overgas Inc, which is half owned by Gazprom, have 8.25 percent each. Bulgaria's biggest state-owned bank Bulbank, and First Private Bank, which is in receivership since May 1996, have 3.2 percent each and the private firm Chimimport two percent.

"In fact the Bulgarian side does not have enough serious presence and this explains the wish of our government to restore the original model of Topenergy or to withdraw from this company together with the Russian side and set up a new venture with 50-50 shares," Bakardzhiev told Standard.
Bulgaria wants to receive Russian gas directly from producer Gazprom, not through an intermediary, as it says this increases the purchase price by $10-15 per 1,000 cubic metres.

Bulgaria has a gas network of more than 2,000 km on its territory and transits Russian gas to Turkey and Greece. Topenergy is prepared to start enlargement of the pipeline between the borders of Romania and Turkey. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
